question: From which of the following instruments is Sarod considered to be derived by the famous sarod player Ustad Amjad Ali Khan?
solution:
The correct answer is__** Rabab**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Point__**

__
 
• **Ustad Amjad Ali Khan Bangash** was born on **October 9, 1945**.
 
• He is an **Indian classical sarod player**, known for his clear and fast **Akhaada Taan**.
 
• He was born into a classical music family and has performed internationally since the 1960s.
 
• He was awarded the **Padma Vibhushan**, India's second highest civilian award, in **2001**.
 
• He first performed in the United States in 1963.
 
• He was awarded the **21st Rajiv Gandhi National Harmony Award**. He received the Padma Shri in 1975, the Padma Bhushan in 1991, and the Padma Vibhushan in 2001.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__** 

 
• **Tar**: A plucked stringed instrument which comes from Persia (present-day Iran). It has a long neck and a double-bowl shape body, played with a plectrum. It has been influential in Persian classical music and is not directly related to the evolution of the Sarod.
 
• **Kamancheh**: A bowed string instrument, similar to a violin, originating from Iran. It has a spherical body and is held upright when played. The Kamancheh is well-regarded in Middle Eastern music but has no direct connection to the development of the Sarod.
 
• **Tambura**: A long-necked plucked string instrument found in Indian classical music, particularly in the supporting role providing a drone in performances. The Tambura has four to six strings and produces a rich, full-bodied sound. It is distinct in function and form from the Sarod and does not contribute to its development.
